messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Sealed environment deployment: post-call recap (Genex Bio)

Hi team,

Quick recap from today’s discovery with Genex Bio (Dr. Amy Liao / Samuel Ortiz). High-level ask: they want Redwood hosted in a fully sealed (air-gapped) environment behind their perimeter, no outbound egress, signed OS images, and strict spare-parting / maintenance processes.

Key constraints we captured:
- No outbound network during normal operations; maintenance via removable media or approved temporary opening windows.
- Only pre-approved OS image (they’ll require cryptographic signing + audit trail).
- Hardware must be on a whitelisted SKU list; customer wants at least 2 spare blades on-site and cold spares for 6 months.
- Upgrade cadence: customer expects major upgrades quarterly, but wants the ability to defer for 30+ days for validation.
- Procurement: they require a vendor security questionnaire, a W-9 equivalent, and a standard PO process with 60-day net.

Immediate asks for us:
1) Provide HW compatibility matrix + recommended spare parts list (owner: Karthik) — due EOD Thu 6/15.
2) Draft a sealed-deploy checklist showing offline upgrade workflow and image signing flow (owner: Priya) — first draft Mon 6/19.
3) Sales to surface procurement constraints and confirm approval gates; prepare a commercial note for Marissa for exceptions (owner: Ben) — by Fri 6/16.

Attachments from call: I’m attaching the Genex follow-up checklist template I started and the notes from the meeting.

Next steps I proposed to the customer: pilot with 1 rack, 2 spare blades on-site, 1 remote spare; 3-month validation window; SOW and procurement checklist to follow. They liked the plan but want formal artifacts before legal/procurement will proceed.

Thanks — short sync 30m tomorrow 9:00am PT to align on owners?

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sealed_deploy_checklist_v1.pdf]
From: Dr. Amy Liao <amy.liao@genexbio.com>

Cc: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@genexbio.com>, procurement <procurement@genexbio.com>

Subject: Re: Sealed environment deployment: post-call recap (Genex Bio)

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the points below and adding a couple clarifications from our side:

1) Network/egress: We cannot have persistent outbound connectivity. Temporary maintenance windows are acceptable but must be pre-scheduled and logged.
2) Image signing: All images deployed in our sealed environment must be signed with a customer-managed key. We have an HSM and will provide a signing endpoint via removable media during setup.
3) Spare parts: We requested two hot spares and one cold spare; any vendor-provided on-site spare must be logged into our inventory system on arrival.
4) Upgrades: We will only allow upgrades after a validation window; rollback procedure must be documented and testable offline.
5) Compliance: We will run a short security questionnaire (we use the standard vendor vendor_assessment_v3.xlsx).

Procurement note: We cannot do Net30. Our PO team requires Net60 and a vendor onboarding packet; I’ve CC’d procurement. Expect a formal vendor questionnaire and a PO once we receive the SOW + compliance artifacts.

If you can send the HW matrix and the sealed-deploy checklist by Thursday, we’ll review and set a procurement timeline.

Regards,
Amy
Dr. Amy Liao
Head of Compute Ops, Genex Bio
[Attachment: vendor_assessment_v3.xlsx]

Ben / Karthik — quick technical clarifications and a proposed pilot plan:

Technical clarifications:
- Image signing: We can support customer-managed signing. Our standard approach: build image in secure build environment -> export image artifact -> customer signs image via provided HSM/offline signing endpoint -> signed image is imported into the appliance. We will add a checksum verification step and write the signature metadata to the on-board audit log.
- Offline upgrades: We support patch bundles delivered via USB or encrypted external media. Upgrade bundles include a pre-check script that runs locally and writes a pre-upgrade snapshot to removable media if configured.
- KV cache warm-up: For first-run cold cache we can ship a pre-warmed cache tarball on media. Note: very large models may require staged warm-up; recommend 48–72 hour warm-up during validation window.

Pilot plan (1-rack minimal):
1) Week 0: Deliver hardware + spares to site; inventory tagging with Genex asset IDs.
2) Week 1: Image signing ceremony (on-site) and import of signed image.
3) Week 2–6: Validation window (traffic replay + performance checks).
4) Week 8: Final acceptance and transition to support cadence.

Risks / blockers:
- Lead times for specific GPU SKUs (we should identify alternatives).
- Internal legal may push on liability for physical spares — recommend drafting a limited liability clause in the SOW.

I’ll draft the image signing diagram and the offline upgrade MOP and attach to the checklist — delivering a first draft by end of day Monday (6/19).

—
